findings.consequence: In the list view, users cannot pause or delete Grafana rules from the actions menu. The Silence entry appears but does nothing. Recording rules lose Pause and Export. This is a functional regression with no authorization bypass.
findings.explanation: The change makes AlertRuleMenu compute canPause, canDelete and canSilence from the Grafana prom-rule abilities, so they can be true when rulerRule is undefined, which is the case in the new list view where the ruler request was removed. The rendering code was not updated. The Pause item requires rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) (lines 123-125), and the Delete item requires rulerRule (line 165). In RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx the SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer only renders when rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) is true (line 104), and rule is undefined in the list view. So Pause and Delete never appear in the list. "Silence notifications" is shown because canSilence is true, but clicking it sets showSilenceDrawer and no drawer renders. Separately, the prom ability set gates Pause, Restore, DeletePermanently and ModifyExport on isAlertingRule, whereas the old code allowed any Grafana-…
findings.title: List-view menu grants prom-rule abilities, but Pause/Delete/Silence actions still require a ruler rule

findings.consequence: The UI shows edit and delete actions on federated rules that the ruler API rejects or that should be read-only. This is a regression from the previous behaviour.
findings.explanation: useAllAlertRuleAbilities used to compute isFederated with isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group). The change makes it delegate to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, which hardcodes isFederated = false (the check is commented out as a TODO). A CombinedRule in a federated external ruler group (for example a Mimir federated group) is therefore no longer treated as immutable. Update, Delete, Pause and Restore are now reported as supported where they were NotSupported. isFederatedRuleGroup still exists in utils/rules.ts, and other callers such as RulesGroup and RuleDetailsButtons still use it, so the old behaviour is intended.
findings.title: Federated rule group check dropped from useAllAlertRuleAbilities

findings.consequence: React emits a missing-key warning. Reconciliation of the Grafana rule items is unstable when the filtered list changes or load-more appends, which can cause wrong item reuse and extra re-renders.
findings.explanation: The `key={key}` prop was dropped when GrafanaRuleLoader was replaced by GrafanaRuleListItem in the `rules.map` callback. The other branches (datasource and default) still pass a key.
findings.title: Missing React key on GrafanaRuleListItem in list map

findings.consequence: In the new list view and in the filter view, which now uses GrafanaRuleListItem, the Silence menu item for Grafana alerting rules is shown but does nothing when clicked.
findings.explanation: The change makes `rule` optional, and GrafanaRuleListItem now renders `<RuleActionsButtons promRule={rule} .../>` with no ruler rule. AlertRuleMenu computes `canSilence` from Grafana prom-rule abilities and shows the Silence item, which calls `handleSilence` and sets `showSilenceDrawer` to true. The drawer only renders when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true, and `rule` is undefined in this case, so nothing appears.
findings.title: Silence action does nothing when only promRule is provided

findings.consequence: Storage and legacy error and latency metrics are wrong. Delete metrics get a high-cardinality label, one value per object name.
findings.explanation: When Storage.Create fails (line 45) and when Storage.Update fails, the code calls recordLegacyDuration(true, ...) instead of recordStorageDuration, so a storage failure is counted as a legacy failure. The legacy goroutine in DeleteCollection calls recordStorageDuration (around line 166) instead of recordLegacyDuration. Delete's success path passes `name` as the kind argument (around line 105) instead of options.Kind.
findings.title: Metrics recorded under the wrong storage label or kind

findings.consequence: In mode 3, legacy storage can silently miss creates, updates and deletes. Legacy and unified storage then diverge. The failures only show up as legacy error metrics.
findings.explanation: In Create (line 51), Delete, Update and DeleteCollection, the goroutine builds its timeout context from the caller's request ctx with context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...). The handler returns right after launching the goroutine, and the API server then cancels the request context. The legacy call therefore runs with an already-cancelled or soon-cancelled context. Legacy writes can then fail with context.Canceled, or never run. The goroutines also use obj, objInfo and options after the handler has returned. A detached context is needed, for example context.WithoutCancel(ctx), before applying the timeout.
findings.title: Async legacy writes inherit the request context and are cancelled when the request returns

findings.consequence: Logs emitted by downstream storage during a delete lack the name, kind and method fields.
findings.explanation: In Delete, `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` is used where the other methods pass the enriched `log`. The name, kind and method values built just above are discarded from the logger that downstream storage reads from the context.
findings.title: Delete sets the context logger to d.Log instead of the enriched log

findings.consequence: Every cleanup cycle writes several Error-level lines per batch. They list every deleted ID, up to AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize of them. This floods the logs and triggers false error alerts. Combined with the cleanup interval dropping from 10 minutes to 1 minute, it happens ten times as often.
findings.explanation: CleanAnnotations (by time, lines 534 and 537, and by count, in the second batch callback) and CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags (the "Tags to clean" and "cleaned tags" lines) call r.log.Error unconditionally on every batch. This happens even when err is nil and nothing failed. Each call logs the whole `ids` slice and the SQL condition. The code looks like leftover debug output. The loop runs until a batch affects zero rows, so every run also logs a final empty batch.
findings.title: Debug logging at Error level on every cleanup batch, including full ID lists

findings.consequence: There is more periodic database load and lock contention. The Error-level logging also fires ten times as often.
findings.explanation: The ticker in CleanUpService.Run changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute. This looks unrelated to the batching change. Every cleanup job now runs ten times as often. That includes the annotation cleanup, which now does a select followed by a delete per batch. clean() allows each run a 9-minute timeout, so a long run can overlap the next tick.
findings.title: Cleanup job interval cut from 10 minutes to 1 minute
